short: Valentinian III stabbed to death the general who had held the western frontiers together for two decades.
full:
On 21 September 454 CE, the western emperor Valentinian III summoned Flavius Aetius, his senior general and the effective ruler of the western empire for over twenty years, to the palace at Ravenna to present financial accounts. Valentinian, egged on by court rivals who feared Aetius's power and his plan to marry his son to the emperor's daughter, drew his sword and killed Aetius himself, with the chamberlain Heraclius joining the attack.

Aetius had held together what remained of Roman Gaul and had led the coalition that checked Attila's invasion of Gaul the previous year; a senator reportedly told Valentinian that he had cut off his right hand with his left. The murder removed the last figure capable of coordinating the west's remaining resources, and Valentinian was himself assassinated by Aetius's former bodyguards within six months, opening a decade of rapid imperial turnover before the west's final collapse.
